perspective:
From Brandon’s perspective, he has access to:

- He is Brandon Talayumptewa, an insurance agent. He meets Benjamin Erickson, an entrepreneur seeking business insurance advice. He is aware Benjamin has limited formal education and worries about explaining complex insurance details clearly.
- First meeting: He heard Benjamin want comprehensive coverage and say some terms were new. Brandon explained liability insurance as a financial safety net, gave a slip-and-fall example, and explained asset protection as covering inventory/equipment. He heard Benjamin ask for an example, say it made sense/simplified things, and thank him.
- Second meeting: He felt more confident after their prior interaction and planned to discuss detailed policy options. He heard Benjamin say he was ready and had been reading up. Brandon explained business interruption insurance and property insurance. He heard Benjamin call these crucial/reassuring.
- Lunch meeting: He felt insecure about being too detailed and wanted to keep discussions engaging. He told Benjamin this. He heard Benjamin appreciate his thoroughness but also enjoy lighter moments. Brandon told a joke about insuring taste buds for a million dollars; Benjamin found it fascinating and sensible. Brandon compared assessing unique risks to Benjamin’s business; Benjamin agreed it was less unusual but equally important.
- Later meeting: He felt pleased by Benjamin’s positive response and decided to offer extra support. He heard Benjamin say his insights had been invaluable. Brandon suggested strategic investments and security upgrades could lower premiums. Benjamin said he hadn’t considered it, called it smart/win-win, and agreed to explore further.
- Joint venture proposal: He felt optimistic and encouraged by their rapport. He proposed co-developing a platform integrating risk management with financial planning for entrepreneurs. Benjamin agreed, called it groundbreaking, and suggested drafting initial plans.
